commons:508911.summary: A shepherd in a short red-brown tunic and leggings stands frontally with a sheep across his shoulders and a staff in his hand, flanked by sheep and goats among sprigs of greenery. Painted on the walls of a Roman catacomb, this pastoral figure was one of the earliest and most beloved ways Christians pictured Christ, who seeks the lost and carries them home.
facts: The Good Shepherd is the most frequently represented image of Christ in early Christian catacomb painting, borrowing the pre-Christian 'ram-bearer' (kriophoros) type.
The Catacombs of Domitilla, on the Via Ardeatina, are one of only a handful of Roman catacombs open to the public.
commons:508911.notes: Commons description is internally inconsistent (says 'circa 350' but dates the file '200–300 CE'); identification as Domitilla rests on the Commons category and a Belmont University web source, not on a museum record. Date given broadly.
